idea-plugin.name: yamlover
idea-plugin.description:
Editor support for the yamlover (.yo) and json5p (.json5p) file types in IntelliJ-based IDEs.

yamlover stands for YAML Overlay (not "Yam lover"): a plain-text, local-first format for knowledge that people and machines can hold together, in one human-readable graph that you edit like notes, an agent reads like a database, and git versions like code. It is close kin to YAML and JSON with first-class pointers, laid over your filesystem: a folder is a mapping, a file is a node, a * pointer is a graph edge.

This plugin gives you:

  • File type recognition for .yo (the legacy .yamlover extension reads forever) and .json5p (JSON5 + pointers), each with its own icon.
  • Syntax highlighting for the COLON grammar: *: a: b references (the pull), ~ reverse edges, & bookmarks (the push), the scope ladder (: document, :: project, ::: world), .. parent, bare-integer positions (: pets: 1; [n] reads as the legacy alias), relative [.±k] indexes, the ~ null key, flat rows (key1: key2: key3: value — every path segment a key, the keyless - / -: segment the sequence marker), flow omni [](), block scalars, quoted keys and comments.
  • YAML-style indentation, two columns and spaces only, as real per-language code style options rather than the IDE's catch-all "Other" defaults. Configurable in Settings | Editor | Code Style.
  • Smart Enter: a block scalar body opens indented under its - > / key: | header and keeps its indent line to line; key: opens its mapping one step deeper.
  • Pointer navigation with Ctrl+click / Ctrl+B: paths, positions, .. and document scope resolve in-file; an overlay file (index.yo or .yo/body.yo) descends the overlaid directory's subdirectories and files, a :: project pointer climbs to the nearest resolving root, and marklower [label](*pointer) links in prose navigate too.
  • Markdown injection: yamlover and json5p fenced code blocks are highlighted inside .md files.

This is deliberately a thin first cut. The grammar is a heuristic reimplementation of the reference parser and navigation is in-file only; a real lexer/PSI and cross-tree link resolution through the yamlover engine are planned.

Documentation (itself written in yamlover, and clickable) · a live instance to try · source on GitHub
